page: Microsoft Azure E96ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the AMD EPYC 7763 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 672.0 GB of RAM, yielding 7.0 GB of memory per core, and includes 3686 GB of local SSD storage alongside Premium Storage capability.

In benchmark testing, the E96ads_v5 demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core CPU tests and PassMark CPU encryption. Its memory subsystem is highly capable, scoring in the top 10% on the PassMark memory score, though uncached large-block read and write memory bandwidth tests fall into the middle 50%. Single-core performance is strong, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores landing in the top 25% and middle 50% respectively.

Given its substantial memory capacity, high-speed local SSD, and strong multi-threaded capabilities, this instance is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale database operations, and data-heavy enterprise applications. It achieves high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require a high memory-to-vCPU ratio without the need for dedicated GPU acceleration.
description: Microsoft Azure E96ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor with 96 vCPUs running at 3.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 672.0 GB of RAM and 3686 GB of local SSD storage. The instance delivers top-tier multi-core CPU and encryption performance, ranking in the top 10% in stress-ng and PassMark benchmarks. Its memory subsystem also registers top-tier scores, though uncached large-block memory bandwidth remains average. With a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 7.0 GB per core and substantial local storage, the E96ads_v5 is designed for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, relational databases, and large-scale data processing tasks where GPU acceleration is not required. It offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads.
